 **The `TOrm` lives in `dom/`, on purpose.** Because the `TOrm` doubles as the domain object ([B.3](#b3-two-types-per-entity-not-three)), it belongs with the domain, not with the persistence machinery. The cost is precise and acceptable: `dom/` depends on the ORM **base type** (`mormot.orm.core`) but never on the ORM **runtime** — no `IRestOrm`, no REST server, no SQL. Those stay in `infra/`. This keeps the dependency direction clean: the port interface in `dom/` can name the entity it returns without reaching into `infra/`, and `infra/` depends on `dom/`, never the reverse. commits.body: ui: pdf - follow-ups to #684: the raster font cache and NewDoc
commits.author: ab

commits.subject: ui: pdf - NewDoc renews the RC4 object key and ends a direct save left open
commits.body: Follow-up to synopse/mORMot2#673 row 7: RC4 caches the key of the last object it encrypted. When the first object the renewed document encrypts has the number of the last one encrypted before - the Info dictionary of a document whose pages are empty - it was encrypted with the key of the old file ID. The writer of a SaveToStreamDirectBegin never ended stayed, and the next save raised "called twice"; FreeDoc frees it, the destructor too.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - the raster font cache is shared by the canvases of a document, and follows its keys
commits.body: Follow-up to synopse/mORMot2#673 row 5: the index an unknown font name was resolved to was cached per canvas, and AddTrueTypeFont cleared only the page canvas, so a form canvas kept the moved index. The cache now lives in TPdfDocument. It also ignored a change of FontFallBackName, and AIsFixedWidth (fixed width takes Courier New), on a single canvas too.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.body:
Following the review: the Appender splits 'schema.table' with the existing
SplitRight(), and dDuckDB is a constant for the PostgreSQL-like dialect, to
be used in the DuckDB code in case a specific dialect is needed one day.

commits.subject: db: DuckDB Appender accepts a schema-qualified table name
commits.body:
The ORM supplies 'main.TableName': the Appender looked for a table named
'main.TableName' in the default schema, so OnBatchInsert failed for tables
whose columns are mapped one to one (found by running the ORM external
tests over DuckDB).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: tf

commits.subject: db: DuckDB integer type list shared by ColumnDouble and ColumnCurrency
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: tf

commits.subject: db: DuckDB logical types are now parsed once into a TDuckDBTypeInfo cache
commits.body:
TDuckDBLogicalType was queried again for every value (type id, decimal
scale, enum dictionary, and a create/destroy of the child type of each
LIST/ARRAY/MAP/STRUCT/UNION row). Parse the column type and its nested
types once, in mormot.db.raw.duckdb (with DuckDBTypeToField and the cached
ENUM dictionary), and use it in the vector to text/JSON conversion.
Numbers, UUID and MAP keys within nested values no longer use a transient
RawUtf8.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: tf

commits.subject: db: DuckDB BindArray removed, OnBatchInsert now uses the Appender
commits.body:
BindArray still executed one statement per row, so it was slower than
plain inserts. TOnBatchInsert is what the ORM uses: implement it with
TSqlDBDuckDBAppender, falling back to MultipleValuesInsert() when the
fields are not all the table columns in order, or for insert options.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: db: release the connection transaction when SharedTransaction() Commit fails
commits.body:
- SharedTransaction() unregisters its entry BEFORE the actual Commit: if the
  Commit failed (e.g. a SQLite3 deferred foreign key, or a lost connection),
  the Zeos and SQLite3 drivers restored their TransactionCount ("still
  active"), and the database transaction could stay open - nobody would ever
  close it, later statements of this connection would run within it, and the
  final Disconnect raised e.g. "You cannot use ROLLBACK in AUTOCOMMIT mode"
- now ReleaseFailedCommit() rolls back our transaction, or only releases our
  level when another transaction is still counted on the same connection
- Zeos and SQLite3 StartTransaction no longer leave TransactionCount
  incremented when the actual database call fails
- new TTestExternalDatabase.SharedTransactionCommitFailure test (fails 8/19
  without the fix)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: Dimitris Kounalakis

commits.subject: net: fixed THttpAsyncServer "Expect: 100-continue" closing the connection
commits.body:
When a request carries "Expect: 100-continue" with a body, DoHeaders()
writes the "HTTP/1.1 100 Continue" interim response before the body is
received. Once this line is written, AfterWrite() is called and took it for
the final response: it released the request body stream, found the state
was not hrsResponseDone, logged "AfterWrite: unexpected" and returned
soClose - so the connection was closed while the client was sending the body.
Any such upload failed, in memory or through OnBodyDownload; curl adds this
header by default for bodies above 1MB.

DoHeaders() now sends the interim response at once from the receiving
thread, with RawWrite() as DoResponse() does for the final response, so it
is never left pending behind the final response (with acoWritePollOnly, a
client sending its body without waiting for the interim response would
otherwise get the final response first, and the connection was closed when
the interim line was eventually flushed), and AfterWrite() is not called
for it. If the OS buffer was full, the remaining bytes go through Write()
and ProcessWrite(): AfterWrite() then recognizes them from the connection
state, since while the request is still being received or processed
(hrsGetBody* up to hrsWaitAsyncProcessing) the final response has not been
set up yet, and it returns soContinue without releasing anything.

Regression test in TNetworkProtocols: uploads with "Expect: 100-continue",
received in memory and through an OnBodyDownload stream, on a default server
and on a server with paoWritePollOnly, several times on the same kept-alive
connection, with and without waiting for the interim response, and a request
without this header.
commits.author: zen010101
